title: Unit-normalized coherent pullback tensor cochain comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and schemes in a universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme]. For a scheme $W$, use its small pro-etale ringed sequence site $\mathbf N\times W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, whose index $n\geq0$ means $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1})_W$, with actual quotient ring maps; put $A_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ and let $\mathscr S_W$ be its category of module sheaves, equivalently strict quotient-semilinear systems [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Write $e_{W,n}$ for exact evaluation, $\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}$ for restriction along $A_W\to B_{W,n}$ and $U_W:\mathscr S_W\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$ for their simultaneous exact scalar restriction. Use ordinary unbounded integer-indexed cochain and derived categories, with localization $q_W$ for $A_W$-modules, $q^s_W$ for sequence modules and $q^t_W$ for towers [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the fixed derived adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, with $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\circ D(U_W)$, and the specified derived tensor and cochain tensor models on the sequence site [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A good integral complex is K-flat with flat terms; K-flat means that its direct-sum total tensor with every acyclic module complex is acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. All comparisons below use the actual chosen adjunctions, not arbitrary isomorphisms between their objects. No boundedness, constructibility, completeness of inputs, or invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes is assumed. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, let $b_f$ on sequence sites be $(n,V)\mapsto(n,X\times_Y V)$. Its ring map is the actual constant-section coefficient map at every $n$; let $f^s_*:\mathscr S_X\to\mathscr S_Y$ be its module direct image, $F_f:\mathscr S_Y\to\mathscr S_X$ its specified left adjoint, $\eta^f$ the unit, and $D_f=D(F_f)$ the exact induced derived inverse image [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Finite module pullback $f_n^*$ is equipped with its actual adjunction unit. The direct-image/evaluation comparison is identity on sections; the fixed inverse-image/evaluation isomorphism $v_{f,n}:f_n^* e_{Y,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}e_{X,n}F_f$ is its inverse mate under the specified finite and sequence adjunctions. Let $\operatorname{Tot}_W$ be the ordinary direct-sum total tensor of unbounded sequence complexes, with the usual signed cochain differential. There exists a unique natural isomorphism
$$z_f:F_f^c\operatorname{Tot}_Y(-,-)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_X(F_f^c(-),F_f^c(-))$$
with the following formula. For any sequence complexes $P,Q$, integers $p,q,k$ with $p+q=k$, object $V=(n,U)$ of the source sequence site, and sections $x\in P^p(V)$, $y\in Q^q(V)$, write $g_{p,q,k,V}(x,y)$ for the pure-tensor generator followed by its total-summand injection, and $\eta^f$ for the actual ordinary sequence adjunction unit on that degree module. Then
$$z^k_{f,P,Q}(b_fV)\bigl(\eta^f_{\operatorname{Tot}_Y(P,Q)^k,V}(g_{p,q,k,V}(x,y))\bigr)
=g_{p,q,k,b_fV}(\eta^f_{P^p,V}(x),\eta^f_{Q^q,V}(y)).$$
The quantifiers include all unbounded complexes and all degrees; no flatness or K-flatness is assumed. This is pullbackTensorSequenceCochain_existsUnique, including naturality, invertibility and uniqueness of the whole cochain natural isomorphism, not only a degreewise module isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $C_W=\mathbf N\times W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $F=F_f$. Check the site hypotheses before using an ordinary tensor theorem. A sequence-site sheaf is precisely a presheaf whose restriction to each vertical slice is a sheaf, since the covering sieves are defined slice by slice. Thus precomposition by $b_f=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf N}\times u_f$ preserves sheaves: on every slice it is the pro-etale direct image. This proves continuity. The functor $u_f$ preserves terminal objects and pullbacks, hence finite limits. For each $T\in X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the category of arrows $T\to u_f(V)$ is cofiltered: for any finite diagram take the limit of its $V$'s and the induced arrow from $T$; the empty diagram uses the terminal object. For $(n,T)\in C_X$, the category of arrows $(n,T)\to b_f(m,V)$ is the product of this category with $(n\downarrow\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf N})$. The latter has initial object $(n,\mathrm{id})$. Choose cones in the two factors to obtain a cone on any finite diagram in the product. This is exactly representable flatness of $b_f$. The sites and all these indices are small in the stipulated module universe.

proof.text:
Use the sequence ring sheaves $R_Y,R_X$ and their specified constant-section structural map $R_Y\to (b_f)_*R_X$. The module direct image is exactly $f^s_*$, with scalar restriction through that map, and $F\dashv f^s_*$ is the specified additive adjunction. Apply the ordinary tensor clause of [lem-sf-site-pullback-tensor-generators] to these sites, rings and this very adjunction. It gives isomorphisms $\mu_{M,N}:F(M\otimes_{R_Y}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}FM\otimes_{R_X}FN$, natural in both module sheaves. Taking the restricted generator with arrow $\mathrm{id}_{b_fV}$ and coefficient $1$ in that theorem gives
$$\mu_{M,N,b_fV}\bigl(\eta^f_{M\otimes N,V}(x\otimes y)\bigr)=\eta^f_{M,V}(x)\otimes\eta^f_{N,V}(y).$$
No choice of a different adjunction or of a finite-evaluation identification enters this application. Only the ordinary tensor clause is used; the theorem's additional K-flat conclusion is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, with the actual-adjunction normalization in lem-sf-site-pullback-tensor-generators

proof.text:
For fixed arbitrary $P,Q$ let $B^{p,q}=P^p\otimes_{R_Y}Q^q$, with its two commuting differentials. For each $k$ the diagonal set $\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=k\}$ is small; its coproduct exists by the total-tensor definition. Since $F$ is a left adjoint, [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] shows that it preserves each of these coproducts. Apply [lem-sfb-left-resolution-map-total-iso] to this bicomplex and the additive functor $F$. It gives a natural chain isomorphism
$$a_B:\operatorname{Tot}(FB)\xrightarrow{\sim}F^c\operatorname{Tot}(B),\qquad a_B^k\iota^{FB}_{p,q}=F(\iota^B_{p,q}).$$
Its inverse therefore satisfies $(a_B^k)^{-1}F(\iota^B_{p,q})=\iota^{FB}_{p,q}$. The cited result applies to all integer-indexed bicomplexes with these diagonal coproducts; no finite diagonal or boundedness assumption has been introduced.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, final total-complex comparison; explicit totalization naturality in the cited mapTotalIso result

proof.text:
Naturality of $\mu$ with the two differentials gives
$$\mu_{P^{p+1},Q^q}F(d_P^p\otimes1)=(Fd_P^p\otimes1)\mu_{P^p,Q^q},\qquad \mu_{P^p,Q^{q+1}}F(1\otimes d_Q^q)=(1\otimes Fd_Q^q)\mu_{P^p,Q^q}.$$
Thus the direct sum of the $\mu_{P^p,Q^q}$ is a chain map $m:\operatorname{Tot}(FB)\to\operatorname{Tot}(F^cP\otimes F^cQ)$: multiply the second displayed equality by $(-1)^p$ and add the first. The direct sum of their inverses is its inverse, since the two composites restrict to the identity on every coproduct summand. The same calculation with a pair of chain maps, using module naturality of $\mu$, proves naturality of $m$ in $P,Q$. Define $z_{f,P,Q}=m\circ a_B^{-1}$; the naturality of $a_B$ and $m$ makes this a natural isomorphism of the two cochain bifunctors in the statement. In every degree it satisfies
$$z^k_{f,P,Q}\,F(\iota^B_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}\mu_{P^p,Q^q}.$$
Every operation takes place in module sheaves on the entire sequence site, so these are also morphisms for all horizontal restrictions.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, constituents of the final comparison; both signed differential summands written explicitly

proof.text:
Write $t_{p,q}(x,y)$ for the pure tensor before its total-summand injection. Naturality of the actual unit for the module map $\iota^B_{p,q}$ gives
$$\eta^f_{\operatorname{Tot}(P,Q)^k,V}(\iota^B_{p,q}t_{p,q}(x,y))=F(\iota^B_{p,q})_{b_fV}\bigl(\eta^f_{P^p\otimes Q^q,V}(t_{p,q}(x,y))\bigr).$$
Apply the summand identity from step 4 and then the unit formula from step 2. The result is $\iota'_{p,q}(\eta^f_{P^p,V}(x)\otimes\eta^f_{Q^q,V}(y))$, which is exactly the displayed generator $g_{p,q,k,b_fV}$ in the statement. This proves the required equation for every integer triple and every site object, including the first quotient level.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, ordinary unit normalization, composed with total-summand injections

proof.text: Let $e$ be any other natural cochain isomorphism satisfying the required equation. Fix $P,Q,k$ and transpose $e^k$ and $z^k$ under the specified $F\dashv f^s_*$; their transposes are $(f^s_*e^k)\eta^f$ and $(f^s_*z^k)\eta^f$, maps from $\operatorname{Tot}_Y(P,Q)^k$ to $f^s_*\operatorname{Tot}_X(F^cP,F^cQ)^k$. The normalization says these maps agree on every pure tensor followed by every summand injection, at every $V$. On one summand, precompose with the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor unit. The resulting linear maps on $P^p(V)\otimes_{R_Y(V)}Q^q(V)$ agree because pure tensors generate the algebraic tensor product. The uniqueness in module sheafification then gives equality on the sheaf tensor summand. The coproduct universal property gives equality of the transposes on the entire degree. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection yields $e^k=z^k$. This holds for all $k,P,Q$, so their chain maps, natural transformations and isomorphisms agree. This proves uniqueness of the whole natural cochain isomorphism.
